source.title: Relief learning is distinguished from safety learning by the requirement of the nucleus accumbens.

confidence_rationale: Direct causal double-dissociation at the substrate level: muscimol inactivation of the nucleus accumbens abolished relief learning but left safety learning intact. This is the strongest available empirical warrant that relief (cessation-contingent) and safety (explicitly-unpaired threat-absence) are neuronally distinct learning processes, which is exactly the premise Q-067 needs before a relief-only / safety-only / both-required decomposition is meaningful. Confidence held below 0.8 by the rodent->REE transfer (startle-potentiation readout, not committed escape action) and by the fact that the paper establishes separability, not which component is the limiting one when a fixed escape bridge is insufficient.
failure_signatures: If a single shared substrate carried both relief and safety, NAC inactivation would have impaired both; instead only relief was abolished, so a substrate that conflates the two (a single escape-credit channel doubling as threat-absence predictor) would be mis-specified.
The dissociation is shown for acquisition under a startle-potentiation readout; it does not by itself demonstrate that the relief component is the missing piece when a directed-escape bridge fails.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Temporary muscimol inactivation of the nucleus accumbens during conditioning abolished relief learning (association of a cue with the cessation/offset of an aversive event) while leaving safety learning (cue explicitly unpaired with the aversive event) intact, showing the two are neuronally distinct forms of learning.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-067 asks whether the structure missing from REE's fixed escape-affordance bridge is relief-only (action/cessation-contingent escape credit, MECH-302/SD-050 -> trainable MECH-375 Q_relief) versus safety-only (prospective threat-absence prediction, MECH-303/304 -> trainable MECH-376 P_safety) versus both. This paper supplies the biological precondition for that question: relief and safety are carried by separable circuits, so building two trainable successors (Q_relief, P_safety) and training the weak one first is substrate-faithful rather than a redundant split of one mechanism.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper demonstrates separability of the two learning types but not a rank ordering of which is rate-limiting; it cannot directly answer the relief-only vs safety-only vs both-required discriminator. The readout is conditioned startle modulation in rats, not a committed instrumental escape action, so the action-contingency that defines REE's relief component is only indirectly engaged.
mapping.source_context: Sprague-Dawley rats; intra-accumbens muscimol; fear-potentiated / relief-modulated acoustic startle paradigm.

confidence_components.notes: Clean causal manipulation with an appropriate control (safety learning preserved), but rodent startle readout and acquisition-only scope raise moderate transfer risk to REE's committed-escape setting.
